## Orientation

Worktree: `/home/andrewyin/se-workflow--dashboard-approvals` (branch `phase/dashboard-approvals`). Write code only under this worktree. Do not edit `.artifacts/`. Do not call `adaptive-artifacts`. Wave-1 peers already landed contract optional note fields (`answer`, `signed_note`, `resolution_note`) and superseded dashboard-read-only constraints — reuse those fields; do not re-do contract or constraint work.

Solo wave-2 task: owns `dashboard/dismiss.py`, `NeedsYouItem.revision` population in `dashboard/model.py`, and approval-focused tests under `-k approval` (argv shapes, reject-does-not-answer, stale refusal). Do not implement the detail-first confirm UX / README keys (that is wave-3 `approval-confirm-ux`).

After code lands, commit on the phase branch excluding `.artifacts`:
`git add -A -- . ':!.artifacts' && git commit -m "approval-dismiss"`

Requirements (quoted):
R4: Approve plan review answers the continuity-question with the note recorded; Reject leaves the question open and writes a record that routes back to discuss/plan (finding `needs: human` or feedback as designed); Sign records `signed_by` and optional note; Accept risk sets `needs: none` with a resolution note.
R5: Writes use the revision of the record as displayed, not `@current`. On stale-revision error, refresh and show that the item changed since opened; no write.
R6: Plan-review items support distinct approve/reject actions (separate keys acceptable).

Design Invariants:
- No write without detail + confirm.
- Reject keeps plan-review blocking.
- Allowed dashboard writes are exactly the human-gate set described by the new constraint.

Design Assumptions:
- Textual modals/pilots can express confirm + note without a new framework.
- Existing dismiss CLI shapes can gain note fields without breaking unsigned flows.

Decisions:
- dashboard-approvals-scope: Full #8: detail, confirm, notes, approve/reject, constraint cleanup
- approval-revision-guard: Writes use the displayed record revision; never @current for these dismissals
